name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: An AI-buildout memory-bottleneck book anchored on Micron (DRAM/HBM) with Sandisk (NAND) cut to a smaller satellite ahead of its October 29 print, and the balance in 4% cash while the chip tape digests AI-financing worries and a priced-in December hike.
reassessment_note: Researched this week (web search and fetches). I still hold the memory-bottleneck thesis, but the tape has turned against beats. SOX is about -15% for October. SOXX fell 6.6% on 10-22 to test its 200-day for the first time in 16 months, after Meta's $135-145B capex raise revived AI-financing worries. Memory sold off that day: SNDK -8%, WDC -7%, MU -6%, with Chinese competition (CXMT) cited. WDC then beat and guided well above consensus ($5.0-5.2B vs ~$4.6B) and still did not rally. SNDK did the same after its August beat (-6.8%). Sandisk reports 10-29 after the close. The leg is already -9.7% against a 20% stop, so a routine sell-the-news move would crystallise the stop on the leg with the richer multiple. I am cutting SNDK from 22% to 12% and keeping MU at 45%. MU is the cheaper and steadier leg, it fell least on 10-22, HBM4 is in volume, and it has no print until December. Fed funds futures put a December hike at 71%, so I keep a large cash buffer rather than adding into it. Re-registering resets each leg's stop to the 10-26 entry, which I accept at the sizes below.

positions.thesis: Micron is the core shovel in AI memory. HBM4 is in high-volume shipments to its lead customer, and fiscal Q4 guidance was about $50B of revenue. In the 10-22 memory selloff it was the mildest decliner (-6% vs -8% SNDK and -7% WDC), and it has no earnings event before December. I keep it at the full 45% because it is the cheapest, highest-quality expression of the DRAM/HBM shortage. The 16% stop caps the damage if the AI-capex rerating becomes a real demand cut.

NAND pricing and enterprise-SSD demand still support Sandisk, whose fiscal Q1 guide was $10.3-10.8B of revenue and $44-46 of EPS, with datacenter revenue doubling. But it reports 10-29 into a tape that sold WDC's beat-and-raise and sold its own August beat. It also carries the richest multiple in the group and is up over 400% YTD. I cut it to 12% so a post-print gap costs about 2% of NAV rather than 4%, while keeping exposure if guidance confirms NAND tightness.
